knowledge_point.title: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression

question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 7 xe^{6 x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =7 x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=7 \\ {v}^{′} & =e^{6 x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{e^{6 x}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 7 x\cdot e^{6 x}\,\text{d}x & =7 x\cdot \frac{e^{6 x}}{6}-\int \frac{e^{6 x}}{6}\cdot 7\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 7 xe^{6 x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 7 xe^{6 x}-\frac{7}{6}\cdot \int e^{6 x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 7 xe^{6 x}-\frac{7}{36}\cdot e^{6 x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Collecting the linear terms gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 7 xe^{6 x}\,\mathrm{d}x & =\frac{7 x e^{6 x}}{6} - \frac{7 e^{6 x}}{36}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (6 x + 7)e^{- 7 x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =6 x + 7\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′} & =e^{- 7 x}\, & ⟹\,v=- \frac{e^{- 7 x}}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (6 x + 7)\cdot e^{- 7 x}\,\text{d}x & =(6 x + 7)\cdot \left(- \frac{e^{- 7 x}}{7}\right)-\int \left(- \frac{e^{- 7 x}}{7}\right)\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (6 x + 7)e^{- 7 x}\,\text{d}x & =- \frac{1}{7}\cdot (6 x + 7)e^{- 7 x}+\frac{6}{7}\cdot \int e^{- 7 x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =- \frac{1}{7}\cdot (6 x + 7)e^{- 7 x}-\frac{6}{49}\cdot e^{- 7 x}+C \\  & =-\frac{(6 x + \frac{55}{7})e^{- 7 x}}{7}+C \\  & =\left(- \frac{42 x + 55}{49}\right)e^{- 7 x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Collecting the linear terms gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (6 x + 7)e^{- 7 x}\,\mathrm{d}x & =\left(- \frac{6 x}{7} - \frac{55}{49}\right)e^{- 7 x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

We need to express $\int (7 x + 1)e^{8 x - 3}\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =7 x + 1\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=7 \\ {v}^{′} & =e^{8 x - 3}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{e^{8 x - 3}}{8}.\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (7 x + 1)\cdot e^{8 x - 3}\,\text{d}x & =(7 x + 1)\cdot \frac{e^{8 x - 3}}{8}-\int \frac{e^{8 x - 3}}{8}\cdot 7\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (7 x + 1)e^{8 x - 3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot (7 x + 1)e^{8 x - 3}-\frac{7}{8}\cdot \int e^{8 x - 3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot (7 x + 1)e^{8 x - 3}-\frac{7}{64}\cdot e^{8 x - 3}+C\end{aligned}

question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (x - 7)e^{x + 5}\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =x - 7\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′} & =e^{x + 5}\, & ⟹\,v=e^{x + 5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (x - 7)\cdot e^{x + 5}\,\text{d}x & =(x - 7)\cdot e^{x + 5}-\int e^{x + 5}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x - 7)e^{x + 5}\,\text{d}x & =(x - 7)e^{x + 5}-\int e^{x + 5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x - 7)e^{x + 5}-e^{x + 5}+C \\  & =(x - 8)e^{x + 5}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Collecting the linear terms gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x - 7)e^{x + 5}\,\mathrm{d}x & =\left(x - 8\right)e^{x + 5}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x5^{x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′} & =5^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{5^{x}}{\ln{(5 )}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot 5^{x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{5^{x}}{\ln{(5 )}}-\int \frac{5^{x}}{\ln{(5 )}}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x5^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5^{x} x}{\ln{(5 )}}-\int \frac{5^{x}}{\ln{(5 )}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\ln{(5 )}}\cdot x5^{x}-\frac{1}{\ln{(5 )}^{2}}\cdot 5^{x}+C \\  & =\frac{5^{x}}{\ln{(5 )}}(x - \frac{1}{\ln{(5 )}})+C\end{aligned}
$$

Collecting the linear terms gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x5^{x}\,\mathrm{d}x & =\left(\frac{x}{\ln{(5 )}} - \frac{1}{\ln{(5 )}^{2}}\right)5^{x}+C\end{aligned}
$$
